target.title: fix: preserve prompt cache prefixes across room-event runs
target.body:
Related: #102175

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes prompt-cache churn in long-lived channel sessions where OpenClaw was changing cache-visible prompt/request prefixes between turns.

The user-visible symptom was same-session provider traces with stable model/cache key but cached prefixes swinging from warm (`~49k-52k`) to much smaller prefixes (`~2k-10k`, later `~37k-40k` ceilings) as room-event, sender-policy, and Responses prompt-boundary details changed the request prefix.

## What Changed

This PR covers three cache invalidators found in the same Discord/channel flow:

1. **Room-event delivery mode vs prompt mode**
   - keeps actual non-internal room-event delivery strict `message_tool_only`
   - adds/threads a prompt-facing delivery mode so system prompts, embedded runs, Codex app-server prompts, dynamic-tool construction, memory/flush runners, and queued followups can use a session-stable prompt contract

2. **Ambient room-event tool inventory**
   - prevents owner/non-owner room-event sender flips from changing cache-visible Gateway tool schemas
   - keeps explicit non-owner execution of owner-only tools blocked
   - preserves the owner-only boundary while avoiding prompt/tool-list churn for ambient room events

3. **Responses prompt cache boundary handling**
   - stops leaking OpenClaw's internal cache-boundary marker into provider payloads
   - preserves no-boundary behavior
   - for standard/custom OpenAI Responses paths that accept post-history instruction messages, keeps the stable prefix before replayed history and appends the dynamic/current-turn suffix after replayed history
   - for the native ChatGPT/Codex Responses backend, keeps the full stripped prompt in top-level `instructions` because live testing showed the backend rejects the split post-history instruction shape with HTTP 400

## Why This Shape

The cache-stable prefix should contain durable instructions and tool schemas. Current-turn routing notes, authorization notes, and other dynamic prompt suffixes should not be prepended ahead of replayed history when the backend accepts a post-history instruction tail.

However, the native ChatGPT/Codex backend has a stricter request contract than the public/custom Responses paths. This PR therefore preserves cache-boundary splitting only where it is request-compatible, while keeping native Codex calls on the accepted top-level `instructions` shape.

This keeps delivery and authorization semantics intact while making cache-visible request prefixes stable for the reporter's long-lived channel sessions where the backend supports it, and avoids bricking native GPT-5.5 Codex OAuth sessions.

## Evidence

Original room-event prompt-mode invalidator:
- Same session/model/cache-key family alternated between automatic-reply prompt text and `message_tool_only` prompt text.
- Prompt-cache reuse varied from near-cold prefixes to warm prefixes despite same provider/model family.
- Source path showed non-internal room events forced effective delivery to `message_tool_only`, and prompt construction consumed the effective mode.

Tool-inventory invalidator:
- Same-session traces differed between `tools=47` and `tools=44`.
- Missing cache-visible tools were `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes`.
- Sanitized gateway log: `[agents/tool-policy] tool policy removed 3 tool(s) via gateway sender owner-only tools.deny: cron, gateway, nodes`.
- After the earlier PR head, live same-session GLM-5.2 traces showed stable `47` tools and cached prefixes around `46.9k-52.2k` on warm turns.

Responses boundary invalidator:
- Later live turns still got low cache even with stable tool inventory.
- Backtrace showed the internal prompt cache boundary was flattened into one pre-history `instructions` string / system prompt message before provider transport.
- The widened tests pin the corrected split shape for compatible Responses paths: stable prefix before input/history, dynamic suffix as the final input item, and no leaked cache-boundary marker.

Native ChatGPT/Codex compatibility regression caught during local install:
- Installing head `66b817d3149` locally caused GPT-5.5 Codex OAuth turns to fail before producing replies.
- Redacted gateway logs repeatedly showed:

```text
[model-fetch] start provider=openai api=openai-chatgpt-responses model=gpt-5.5 method=POST url=https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
[model-fetch] response provider=openai api=openai-chatgpt-responses model=gpt-5.5 status=400 contentType=application/json
[responses] error provider=openai api=openai-chatgpt-responses model=gpt-5.5 message=400 status code (no body)
embedded_run_agent_end error="LLM request failed." rawErrorPreview="400 status code (no body)"
```

The regression lined up with the native ChatGPT/Codex provider appending the cache-boundary dynamic suffix as an input `developer` message. Current head `b8a181bc694` restores the accepted native request shape while keeping the split contract for compatible Responses paths.

Private user IDs, channel IDs, hostnames, API keys, and full trace identifiers are intentionally omitted.

## Current Head Validation

Head: `b8a181bc694841ca142db04b95106cf9c7db2b16`.

- Targeted payload regression pack: `pnpm vitest run packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts --testNamePattern "cache-boundary|Codex responses"` — **3 files, 11 tests passed**.
- Full relevant Responses regression pack: `pnpm vitest run src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts` — **4 files, 656 tests passed**.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `pnpm build` — passed.
- Local install smoke: rebuilt and installed current head into LaunchAgent; gateway reports running with connectivity probe OK and admin-capable.
- Post-restart log check from the restart point showed no new `status=400` / `400 status code` entries. Fresh provider-cache proof from a new live turn is still pending.

Earlier focused validation on this PR also covered room-event delivery mode, owner-only tool execution boundaries, queued followups, embedded runners, Codex app-server prompts, dynamic-tool prompt mode, memory/flush runners, and no-marker-leak payload assertions.
